purpose: Provider boundary and transport mutation coverage. H01 pins dependency direction. H02 observes the exact provider failure class at the Step boundary. Z01-Z06 cover wire keys, dependency declarations, HTTPS, tool decoding, bounded capture allocation, and terminal authentication failure. Z07-Z17 cover incremental UTF-8, EOF and CRLF framing, block ordinals, capacity release, and exact dependency features. Z18-Z32 cover shared transport, credentials, capture settlement, and physical-attempt identity bounds. Runtime-owned vocabulary rows remain in the runtime manifest.
isolation: Every mutation is applied in its own disposable worktree at the exact committed candidate. The calling worktree remains unchanged. Each row also builds into its own deterministic target directory under the run root, named for the row id. The ambient CARGO_TARGET_DIR and CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR -- which the Linux heavy-gate profile exports for every route -- are stripped from every cargo child rather than overridden, so one row's artifacts can neither decide nor forge the next row's verdict, and a bounded recursive path/type/size fingerprint before and after the battery shows the ambient directory received nothing.
scope_note: Only deletable behavior seams receive mutation rows. The distinction between AttemptTerminalReason and StepTerminalReason is carried by compile-fail probes 70/71. ProviderEnded, ContextFailure, AuthorityRefused, DurabilityFailure and ProcessLoss are not produced by the attempt-to-Step conversion, so no rows claim to cover them. Probe 04 carries the Codex request type boundary; Z01 checks its serializer instead.
prefix_note: This manifest owns the whole mutation prefixes H, Z and PR. Match complete prefixes: PR must never be interpreted as P. Pack names and evidence_label values are stable runner selectors and report identifiers. PR11-PR13 are rustdoc rows whose command is fixed by the runner; rejection requires the exact diagnostic under warnings-as-errors, not an arbitrary nonzero exit.
